This page records the existing DHIS2–GESIS mapping-cleaning workflow without
changing its code. The stage boundaries separate session setup, source reads,
reviewed corrections, validation queries, and persistence so each part can be
made reproducible and target-oriented independently.

::: {.callout-warning title="Legacy code preserved for staged modernization"}

The code below is intentionally unmodified. It contains interactive-session
state, relative paths, mutable objects, diagnostic expressions, and a direct
write. Treat each procedure as a modernization boundary rather than as an
endorsement of its current implementation. Preserve the reviewed mapping
decisions while changing execution mechanics only after their behavior has
been characterized.

:::

::: {.manual-prereq title="Retain The Reviewed Source Evidence"}

The original mapping CSV and the four manually reviewed workbooks or CSVs
must remain available with their provenance intact. Before optimizing a stage,
record its input schema, expected row-count change, join cardinality, and the
review decision represented by each correction.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Initialize The Legacy Session And Read The Mapping"}

This stage reads the base mapping, and assigns names to the four UID levels.
It removes the year 2022 and Belelanda from the list.

```{r}

crosswalk_mapping_df <- read.csv(pipeline_raw_crosswalk_file) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename(region_uid = UID, 
         district_uid = `UID.1`,
         commune_uid = `UID.2`, 
         fs_uid = `UID.3`) |>
  filter(cAnnee != "2022" & code_fs != "Belalanda") %>%
  verify(nrow(.) == 34812)  
```


:::



::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 2 — Correct Out-Of-Range GESIS Codes"}

This stage loads the reviewed corrections, checks UID consistency for both the
old and corrected codes, and then applies the corrected GESIS code.

```{r}
# 2) bits out of range ------
# Some clinic GESIS codes have the type or public/private bits out of the expected range, 
# sometimes, those GESIS codes should be corrected 
pipeline_raw_gesis_correct_path <- str_subset(pipeline_raw_input_files_paths, "CSB1 CSB2 PUBLIC PRIVATE.xlsx")

crosswalk_gesis_correct_df <- read_xlsx(pipeline_raw_gesis_correct_path) |>
  filter(!is.na(`NEW CODE`) & `NEW CODE` != "NEW CODE") %>% 
  setNames(c("old_code", "correct_code", "uid", "name", "status", "note")) %>% 
  unique()

# double check what fixing these GESIS codes will do
# A) do any clinics already have the corrected GESIS codes? if so, do they have the same UID? 
crosswalk_mapping_df %>% 
  left_join(crosswalk_gesis_correct_df %>% select(code_fs = correct_code, new_uid = uid)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(new_uid)) %>% 
  filter(new_uid != fs_uid) %>%
  nrow 
# yes, and the uid always matches 

# B) does the uid also match the one for the old code?
crosswalk_mapping_df %>% 
  left_join(crosswalk_gesis_correct_df %>% rename(code_fs = old_code, new_uid = uid)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(new_uid)) %>% 
  filter(new_uid != fs_uid) %>%
  nrow
# yes, the updated uid matches the one from the old code, so shouldn't affect UID contiguity for a clinic

# make the adjustment to the mapping file
crosswalk_mapping_corrected_df <- crosswalk_mapping_df %>% 
  left_join(crosswalk_gesis_correct_df %>% select(code_fs = old_code, correct_code), 
            by = c("code_fs")) %>% 
  mutate(code_fs = ifelse(is.na(correct_code), code_fs, correct_code)) %>% 
  select(-correct_code) %>%
  #manual fill the UID from other years for 630151027
  mutate(fs_uid = ifelse(code_fs == "630151027" & grepl("Ankilivalo", FS), 
                         "ZX5EkF6eC0x", 
                         fs_uid)) 

```


:::


::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 4 — Fill Missing UIDs From The Reviewed Workbook"}

This stage imports reviewed UID fills and applies them by GESIS clinic code.

```{r}
# 4) fill in missing UIDs for GESIS-years in mapping ----
# for GESIS-years for public clinics in the mapping file
# reporting data in 2018/2019 using this file for those 4 clinics 
uid_fill_path <- str_subset(pipeline_raw_input_files_paths, "gesis_missing_uid_in_mapping.xlsx")

uid_fill_df <- read_xlsx(uid_fill_path) %>% 
  mutate(code_fs = as.character(code_fs))

crosswalk_mapping_uids_df <- crosswalk_mapping_corrected_df %<>% 
  left_join(uid_fill_df %>% select(code_fs, uid), 
            by = "code_fs") %>% 
  mutate(fs_uid = ifelse(is.na(uid), fs_uid, uid))  %>% 
  select(-uid)
# no GESIS changes, so only concern for this change is if there are other clinics 
# with the same UID --> only one of the UIDs filled in is otherwise in the 
# mapping file, and it appears to be the same clinics in the mapping 
# in the diagnosis dataset, there's a clinic in that same commune that has data 
# for earlier years that seems like its the same "Antanisoa", but it was private
# BUT the GESIS code for that clinic 120143040 also has another name "CMC Ambararata Est", 
# which seems to correspond to when the commune changes for that clinic 
# this clinic was not captured in our 21 GESIS - UIDs with concerning name changes 
# because it was private over that time span
```

The future implementation should validate uniqueness on the join key and
retain the narrative evidence associated with these reviewed exceptions.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 5 — Reconcile UID-Years With Multiple GESIS Codes"}

This stage classifies reviewer notes, retains the original internal diagnostic
as comments, evaluates external GESIS–UID consequences, and applies deletions
and renames.

```{r}
# 5) UID-years with multiple GESIS codes ---- 
mult_gesis <- read.csv("./data/raw/symphonia_verified/VERIFIER fs_uid_year_with_multiple_gesis.csv") %>% 
  mutate(change = case_when(grepl("the clinic was moved to the district of mandoto", note) ~ "keep", 
                            note %in% c("Same clinic", "OK", "ok") ~ "keep", 
                            grepl("^rename", note) ~ "rename", 
                            grepl("delete|Delete", note) ~ "delete",
                            T ~ as.character(NA)), 
         code_fs = as.character(code_fs)) 
# started with 36 UID-years with multiple GESIS 
# there are 2 deletions, 16 renames, and 18 cases where its just two codes for the same clinic
# --> 18 UID-years with multiple GESIS at the end

# what will the impacts of this correction be? 
# internally, for any UIDs that we're correcting, check what happens
# mapping %>% 
#   left_join(mult_gesis %>% 
#               select(cAnnee, code_fs, change, 
#                      fs_uid_correct = UID, 
#                      fs_name_correct = `NAME.CLINICS`), 
#             by = c("cAnnee", "code_fs")) %>% 
#   filter(change != "delete" | is.na(change)) %>% 
#   mutate(fs_uid_correct = case_when(change == "rename" & fs_uid_correct == "No UID" ~ "",
#                                     change == "rename" ~ fs_uid_correct, 
#                                     T ~ fs_uid),
#          FS_correct = case_when(change == "rename" & fs_name_correct != "" ~ fs_name_correct, 
#                                 T ~ FS)) %>% 
#   group_by(fs_uid_correct) %>% 
#   filter(any(change == "rename")) %>% 
#   filter(fs_uid_correct != "") %>% 
#   arrange(fs_uid_correct) %>% 
#   View
# all seems reasonable

# externally, will this change GESIS - UID pairs? only for times when there is a UID added, 
# dropping a UID to blank shouldn't have an effect since the GESIS is unchanged
mapping %>% 
  left_join(mult_gesis %>% 
              select(cAnnee, code_fs, change, 
                     fs_uid_correct = UID, 
                     fs_name_correct = `NAME.CLINICS`), 
            by = c("cAnnee", "code_fs")) %>% 
  filter(change != "delete" | is.na(change)) %>% 
  mutate(fs_uid_correct = case_when(change == "rename" & fs_uid_correct == "No UID" ~ "",
                                    change == "rename" ~ fs_uid_correct, 
                                    T ~ fs_uid),
         fs_name_correct = case_when(change == "rename" & fs_name_correct != "" ~ fs_name_correct, 
                                T ~ FS)) %>% 
  filter(fs_uid_correct != "") %>% 
  group_by(fs_uid_correct) %>% 
  mutate(uid_change = any(change == "rename")) %>% 
  group_by(code_fs) %>% 
  mutate(gesis_change = any(uid_change)) %>% 
  filter(uid_change) #%>% 
  #View
# main concern is GESIS - UID pairs that are now more years, so would include more names in the diagnosis data 
# following UID should be checked: 
# 630241019 - UiaPcR9m5R8 adding old 2015 -- CSB2 Manevy (good)
# 530541020 - EB8qTcx1zZb adding 2017 -- CSB1 Manankatafana (good)
# in the diagnosis data, both have no major name changes

# make the change 
mapping %<>%
  # the UIDs got dropped when we rename, which only matters in one case 
  # whe the row needs to be deleted, so separately add in the delete cases vs rest
  left_join(mult_gesis %>%
              filter(change == "delete") %>% 
              select(cAnnee, code_fs, fs_uid, change),
            by = c("cAnnee", "code_fs", "fs_uid")) %>%
  filter(change != "delete" | is.na(change)) %>% 
  select(-change) %>% 
  left_join(mult_gesis %>%
              filter(change != "delete") %>% 
              select(cAnnee, code_fs, change,
                     fs_uid_correct = UID,
                     fs_name_correct = `NAME.CLINICS`),
            by = c("cAnnee", "code_fs")) %>%
  mutate(fs_uid = case_when(change == "rename" & fs_uid_correct == "No UID" ~ "",
                            change == "rename" ~ fs_uid_correct,
                            T ~ fs_uid),
         FS = case_when(change == "rename" & fs_name_correct != "" ~ fs_name_correct, 
                        T ~ FS)) %>%
  select(-(change:fs_name_correct))
# deletes 2 rows, so now down to 34810 
# check that there are ony 18 UID-years mapping to 2 GESIS codes
# mapping %>% 
#   filter(fs_uid != "") %>%
#   group_by(fs_uid, cAnnee) %>% 
#   summarise(n_gesis = n_distinct(code_fs)) %>% 
#   filter(n_gesis > 1) %>% 
#   nrow
```

Modernize the classification, impact analysis, and mutation as separate
targets or pure functions so reviewer decisions can be checked before they
alter the mapping.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 6 — Add Reviewed GESIS Codes Missing From The Mapping"}

This stage constructs the accepted missing clinic across eight mapping years
and appends those rows.

```{r}
# 6) 10 GESIS codes not in the mapping ----
# 8 need to be deleted from diagnosis data, 1 doesn't have a UID, lets add row for the last 1
uid_add <- read.csv("./data/raw/symphonia_verified/VERIFIER clinic_codes_in_gesis_but_not_in_mapping.csv") %>% 
  filter(NOTE != "DELETE" & uid != "NO UID") %>% 
  left_join(data.frame(cAnnee = c("2013", "2015", "OLD GESIS 2015", 
                                  "NEW GESIS 2015", "2016", "2017", "2018", "2019")), 
            by = character()) %>% 
  transmute(cAnnee, 
            code_reg = NA, 
            region_uid = NA, 
            region = NA, 
            code_dist = NA, 
            district_uid = NA, 
            district = NA, 
            code_commune = NA, 
            commune_uid = NA, 
            commune = NA, 
            code_fs = as.character(clinic_code), 
            fs_uid = uid, 
            TYPE = str_split_fixed(name, " ", 2)[,1],
            FS = name) 

mapping %<>% 
  rbind(uid_add)
# adds 8 rows --> 34818
```

Future work can make the intended one-clinic/eight-year expansion and output
schema explicit before replacing the cross join and row binding.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 7 — Apply Remaining Manual Corrections"}

This stage contains the remaining UID- and year-specific substitutions,
deletions, and additions discovered while integrating the mapping with the
diagnosis data.

```{r}
# 7) some manual changes ---- 
# integrating the mapping with the diagnosis dataset identified these problems with the mapping file
mapping %<>% 
  mutate(code_fs = case_when(fs_uid == "naW8NwTF6iT" & cAnnee == "NEW GESIS 2015" ~ "430351007",
                             fs_uid == "C43g5TA5l3j" & grepl("2015", cAnnee) ~ "430351006",
                             fs_uid == "hVmE01gCHfg" &
                               cAnnee %in% c(2013:2019,
                                             "NEW GESIS 2015",
                                             "OLD GESIS 2015") ~ "220441038",
                             fs_uid == "i9IyexSemHX" ~ "220441034",
                             fs_uid == "xWIEcSCmwUF" & cAnnee == "2010" ~ "440551024",
                             fs_uid == "QxMf9Q2KYxI" & cAnnee == "2010" ~ "440541010",
                             T ~ code_fs)) %>% 
  # replace what 340141015 is mapping to in new 2015, easier to delete one row and add another
  {rbind(filter(., !(fs_uid == "H9S6IOY4CKL" & code_fs == "340141015" & cAnnee == "NEW GESIS 2015")),
         filter(., fs_uid == "SnRMbMj7ON9" & cAnnee == "OLD GESIS 2015") %>%
           mutate(cAnnee = "NEW GESIS 2015",
                  code_fs = "340141015"))} %>%
  # similarly, replace what 520551034 is mapping to in 2011 - old 2015
  {rbind(filter(., !(fs_uid == "JnmokyKVSvS" & code_fs == "520551034" & 
                            cAnnee %in% c(2011:2014, "OLD GESIS 2015"))),
         filter(., fs_uid == "d0n2W7psb6s" & cAnnee == "2016") %>% 
           mutate(code_fs = "520551034") %>% 
           select(-cAnnee) %>% 
           left_join(data.frame(cAnnee = c(2011:2014, "OLD GESIS 2015")), 
                     by = character()))} %>% 
  # add row for "H9S6IOY4CKL" in new 2015  
  {rbind(., 
         filter(., fs_uid == "H9S6IOY4CKL" & cAnnee == "OLD GESIS 2015") %>%
           mutate(cAnnee = "NEW GESIS 2015",
                  code_fs = "340141014"))} %>% 
  # drop rows for UID noCoZFMcMVa in 2010, 2011, old 2015
  filter(!(fs_uid == "noCoZFMcMVa" & cAnnee %in% c(2010, 2011, "OLD GESIS 2015")))
  # nrow # reduces from 34819 to 34816 rows
                             
```

Each exception should eventually be represented as auditable correction data
or as a narrowly named rule, with before/after assertions for its affected
records.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Stage 8 — Check Mapping Cardinality And Names"}

These diagnostics examine UID-year-to-GESIS multiplicity, newly introduced
GESIS-to-UID multiplicity, and UIDs associated with multiple clinic names.

```{r}
# 8) checks ---- 
# how many cases of uid-year mapping to multiple GESIS?
mapping %>% 
  group_by(fs_uid, cAnnee) %>% 
  summarise(n_gesis = n_distinct(code_fs)) %>% 
  filter(fs_uid != "") %>% 
  filter(n_gesis > 1)  %>% 
  nrow
# 18 from before + we made another one for UID HsLE6ajNRZX in 2017 with our 
# recent addition in 6, but both codes show up in the diagnosis dataset in 2017

# how many gesis map to more than one uid that didn't before?
mapping %>% 
  group_by(code_fs) %>% 
  summarise(n_uid = n_distinct(fs_uid)) %>% 
  filter(n_uid > 1)  %>% 
  pull(code_fs) %>% 
  setdiff(read.csv("./data/raw/from Symphonia/mapping GESIS DHIS questions - mapping DHIS2 GESIS 2010 2022.csv") %>%
            rename(region_uid = UID, 
                   district_uid = `UID.1`,
                   commune_uid = `UID.2`, 
                   fs_uid = `UID.3`) %>% 
            group_by(code_fs) %>% 
            summarise(n_uid = n_distinct(fs_uid)) %>% 
            filter(n_uid > 1)  %>% 
            pull(code_fs))

# "110543027" "120143023" "520543054" "530541020" "530651023" "610143024" "640352018"
# first two clinics (and their UID) seems like a bit of a mess, but its FSP so maybe we don't care 
# for the public ones
# "530541020" --> seems the codes got messed by between two clinics and this fixes it 
# "530651023" --> same as above? much shorter time series for all gesis/uid involved

# does each UID have one name? 
mapping %>% 
  group_by(fs_uid) %>% 
  mutate(n_name = n_distinct(FS)) %>% 
  filter(fs_uid != "") %>% 
  filter(n_name > 1) #%>% View
# 2 cases where thats not true, but both reflect a change in clinic type
```

During modernization, convert the accepted counts and exception sets into
explicit tests while retaining inspectable diagnostic tables for unexpected
records.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Persist The Clean Mapping"}

The legacy workflow ends by writing the cleaned mapping directly to an
intermediate CSV.

```{r}
# save the clean mapping file ----
write.csv(mapping, "./data/intermediate/mapping_gesis_dhis2_clean.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)
```

The final modernization boundary can replace this side effect with a declared
file target after all preceding transformations and checks have reproducible
interfaces.

:::
